data.narrative:
Mission Zero Technologies is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nicholas Chadwick, Shiladitya Ghosh, and Gaël Gobaille-Shaw, having raised £21.8M to date. The valuation exercise is informed by a peer universe spanning one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private-sector peers in climate and energy, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using the £21.8M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of £44M. Peer-median triangulation could not be reliably applied due to insufficient datapoints: while eight same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more comparables meeting narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier. Using an all-sector median would introduce material bias and has been excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of £37M to £50M, with a median point of £44M. This single-method triangulation reflects the inherent limitation of sparse, early-stage comparable data in frontier climate tech. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x stage-progression multiplier for this subsector, the lack of direct peer benchmarking, and changes to capital markets conditions since the £21.8M raise.
